Antistrophe 3. versuum 8.
AB equorum studio, pietate in deos, & hospitalitate.
Ἱπποτροφίας π.) Decima laus ab equestribus studiis:
Erat autem Græcis communis lex, qua ditioribus neces-
sum erat equos alere, ad patriæ utilitatem.
Καὶ ξένων ξενίας.) Undecima laus ab hospitalitate: ventus
nunquam contraxit vela circa mensam, hoc est, nunquam
parcus in peregrinos fuit nunquam tenax. Sequitur distri-
butio a temporum circunstantia: æstate ad Phasin vsque,
hyeme vero ad Nilum Ægypti suos conuiuas extulit. Pha-
sis Scythiæ fluuius frigidus: Nilus contrà Ægypti calidus
fluuius. æstate ad Phasin deduxit, hoc est, loca suffrigida
præbuit, refectioni idonea: Hyeme contrà ad Nilum, hoc
est, calentia loca præbuit: eleganti allegoria ostendens,
quæsiuisse omnes occasiones, vt opportunè amicis grata
exhiberet.

page.notes: Greek citations and some Greek words are doubtful at this scan resolution (e.g. the lead-in of the first Antistrophe paragraph, Ὅτιν ὀρχάν, ἀιδοῖος ἀσφῶς, Καὶ ξένων ξενίας, and Μὴ νῦν). They are transcribed as best read but carry no [?] marks; they should be checked against a higher-resolution image. The Latin is complete. Printed spelling such as "Epenthelis", "Octaua" and "contrà" is kept as printed. Long s is plain s throughout. The printed "vt" and "conuersatione" are normalised to "ut" and "conversatione" under the u/v rule.
